answer: Each agent gets a scarce, nontransferable enrollment credential only after a live person completes a liveness check and a randomly assigned task; the credential is then bound to a hardware-backed key used to sign economic actions. A willow-patterned task on the knoll may be followed by a zephyr-themed one, so scripted repetition fails. An attacker must recruit real people or repeatedly pass costly checks, rather than minting identities for free, and loses access if credentials are detected as duplicated.
